scope: Eight independent Bun.WebView 1.4.2 Linux Chrome launches, seven native fixture categories, one worker, three warmups and twelve measured operations per category. One separate native control excluded from statistics. No cross-engine ratios or equivalent-work admission.

acceptance.rationale: Require at least a 10% complete-flow improvement with a launch-clustered confidence interval excluding parity. Reject median regressions above 5%, observed tail regressions above 15%, and memory growth above 10% unless explicitly reviewed. Baseline-only data establishes variability; it cannot pass a speed comparison. Tail claims need the stated sample counts.

configuration.exclusionPolicy: Retain every attempted launch and sample. Unexpected errors invalidate a comparison, not individual slow observations. Only an explicitly documented external interruption can invalidate an entire run. Never rerun selectively.
configuration.executionOrder: Rotate workloads by launch index; paired engine comparisons must alternate which engine starts each launch pair.
configuration.resourceCoverage: External watchdog samples the observed descendant process tree, including separately grouped browser processes. Short-lived processes between samples may be missed; report this limitation.

timing: Operation intervals include native calls and assertions. Setup includes fresh-view creation, navigation, predicate and unacknowledged view-close request. Other preparation/observation/close intervals are separate. Command-through-drain includes fixture service, executable/source checks, report serialization and all observed descendant drain; hashes warm file caches, so this is not cold startup.

nativeLaunchPolicy.argumentsEvidence: Pinned source expectations only; proc cmdline may be an overwritten process title and does not authenticate original argv.

classifications.name: backend
reasons: Native Chrome launch flags, live executable identity, input/readiness, context isolation and cleanup need original collector controls.
Text uses a declared evaluate/MutationObserver helper; this is not a native assertion API.
Native click + Home + Shift+End + InsertText differs from locator.fill; retain extra key/input events and independent server counts.
High-level navigate has no HTTP response result; response status admission remains separate.

classifications.name: failure
reasons: Native Chrome launch flags, live executable identity, input/readiness, context isolation and cleanup need original collector controls.
Native selector-click actionability timeout differs from the reference visibility/assertion failure and diagnostics.

limitations: Different native launch flags, shared default browser context, text assertion helper, backend replacement keys and native click-timeout failure prevent an equivalent-work ranking against the historical table.
The native closeAll operation SIGKILLs Chrome. Native descendants are adopted; all strict-clean-custody flags remain false even when drain completes without collector intervention.
Original wrapper wait, adopted waits and cgroup charges remain distinct. Charged peak memory is not concurrent RSS. Requested limits do not establish full policy/exclusive-membership admission.
Source/executable hashes bind selected declared inputs, not loaded-library identity or original browser argv. The proc/native-source limitation remains.
96 measured operations per category are below the configured p95/p99 sample minimums; no tail estimates or leadership claims.

The measured sampler metadata says close requests are separate; setup actually includes its close request in each sample. This wording is corrected after the campaign without changing numeric boundaries or rerunning workloads.
